thread_analysis.thread_summary: Sharp Corporation (contacts Yoshio Iwai, Hiroshi Sunaga, earlier Shinya Higashi) engages Allion (Itsuo Sakai) on Bluetooth certification strategy for products using open-source BlueZ or generic Bluetooth dongles, spanning May 2023 through October 2025 across two related sub-projects (an earlier unnamed project and a new projector project). The thread is unusually rich in generalizable, reusable strategic guidance around uncertified host stack risk, generic-dongle registration scoping, and certification-timeline-vs-launch-schedule decoupling.
all_questions_found: Does a projector using a generic, unspecified third-party Bluetooth USB dongle need to be registered the same way as a precedent involving a dedicated bundled dongle? (see thread_0046_case_01)
Can an unrelated third party's existing registered QDID be referenced for a new registration, and what is the realistic risk profile of implementing raw open-source BlueZ? (see thread_0046_case_02)

Does a certified Host Subsystem stack eliminate all testing, even for a surface-mount module with PCB-trace-routed antenna feed, and does host OS choice (Linux vs. Android) matter for RF testing? (see thread_0046_case_03)
Can a product launch without Bluetooth support and add/certify it later via a running-change firmware update before marketing Bluetooth compatibility? (see thread_0046_case_04)

(Unresolved/not directly answered in visible content) An earlier (2023) question about whether a Windows PC with Bluetooth hardware disabled at shipment (requiring user driver installation) needs End Product registration, and whether the OS-embedded host stack can reference an existing QDID -- the consultant's answer to this specific question is not visible in this thread excerpt.
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: This thread provides an unusually complete, real-world risk picture for the open-source BlueZ implementation path: a concrete ~60% first-pass rate, ADB-debugger-plus-bilingual-on-site-engineer requirement, ~3-month timeline, and several-million-yen cost range, reinforced by the explicit cross-reference that a related Sharp team ultimately abandoned raw BlueZ after hearing this same risk profile. Case_01's generic-dongle-vs-dedicated-accessory registration distinction and case_04's running-change/launch-decoupling strategy are both previously undocumented, high-value strategic patterns.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: See thread_0046_case_01 through thread_0046_case_04 for case-specific decision logic.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: See individual case files; case_02 carries the highest risk of wasted development effort if a customer commits to raw open-source BlueZ without understanding the realistic pass-rate and cost profile, while case_04's running-change strategy, if misapplied, could result in premature Bluetooth-compatible marketing claims before the later registration is actually public.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: No significant consulting-side mistakes identified -- the consultant consistently and proactively shared the same detailed open-source BlueZ risk profile across multiple separate customer engagements (departments) within the same company, and offered the running-change strategy as a creative solution once the customer's own analysis concluded the uncertified-stack timeline wouldn't meet their schedule.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When a customer proposes implementing raw open-source BlueZ (or any uncertified host stack), proactively share the realistic pass-rate, cost, and timeline risk profile based on past engagements rather than just confirming technical feasibility, and offer the certified-commercial-stack-vendor list as a lower-risk alternative; separately, when a customer's certification timeline doesn't fit their production schedule, the running-change strategy (launch without the feature, add and certify it later) is a legitimate way to decouple the two, governed by the simple rule that new registration is triggered specifically by ICS-table-support additions, not by software changes in general.
